surveys.stateOfGame:
LOOP AS CODED. Summon costs 100 gems, has no roster cap (game.js:754-788) and shows one card that the next pull replaces (game.js:2659-2666). Town staffing is automated: 'Optimal jobs' (game.js:1710), the rota (game.js:637-681) and 'Hone' (game.js:1699) leave a few clicks per hour. There are two mission systems. The Gate (14 fixed zones, missions.js:75-90) resolves on town ticks with no input after launch, writes state.missions.done (missions.js:276), and has a debrief (game.js:2346-2360). The Field (sortie.js, 16 contract types) runs live on a map, and its contract level is read from the Gate's clears (sortie.js:42-50). The Field player decides which of 5 contracts (board rolls every 6 min, or at once through a free 'Ask around' button, sortie.js:22, 1006-1011) and which party. During a run the only controls are speed, camera, Skip, 'Fall back' (defence contracts only) and 'Call it off' (sortie.js:1264-1271). Advancement trials (quests.js) and the altar (game.js:2411) are the two other sinks for characters.

SCARCITY. Gems are not the constraint. Measured in Node: mean maintenance output is 1.22 gems/tick per character before rest, morale and temper factors (4000 sampled pulls), which is about 4.9 gems/min per worker at the 2/3 duty cycle (game.js:513-514). A level-3 contract averages 228 gems (40 rolls per type through MT.roll, payout formula sortie.js:479) over 3.05 min of real time at 1x, about 75 gems/min for the party, versus about 20 gems/min for the same four on maintenance. Skip (sortie.js:404-414) plus the free reroll make that ratio limited only by clicks. The scarce things are therefore people and attention, which makes consequences to people the main lever on engagement.

WHAT A SORTIE COSTS THE PEOPLE ON IT. Survivors pay nothing: sortie.js settle() (439-541) never calls Condition.spend (the Gate does, missions.js:259) and never sets c.injured. c.injured has about 15 consumers (party pickers, rota, trials, morale, town map, roster tile) and no producer in the browser: its only writer, missions.js:266, sits in the branch for Roster being undefined, and roster.js is loaded (game.html:520). Death is also optional: 'Call it off' (sortie.js:338-350) frees the whole party without checking who is down, while Roster.fall runs only inside settle() (sortie.js:450). Aptitude xp and bestiary entries earned during the run are kept (sortie.js:177, 181). In the plain-attrition harness at POW 0.6, 14.3% of runs contain a death and only 5.7 points of runs are both won and contain a death, so abandoning at the first death keeps every life and costs about 6% of payouts.

WHAT THE PLAYER CANNOT SEE OR KEEP. The Field has no debrief. Bestiary.record already builds per-fight encounter blocks on the run object (bestiary.js:95-106), but persist() omits them (sortie.js:299-302), 'Back to the board' discards the run (sortie.js:1281) and Report.renderRun is only called for Gate runs. A character has no history: no c.record field exists, the memorial stores name, stars, cause, time served and top aptitudes (roster.js:95-105), and Bonds.mourn deletes the dead's bonds (bonds.js:240-246) after at most four log lines (game.js:384). Temper axes are written once at roll (temper.js:154-160; no other writer). Sacrifice (sacrifice.js:177-181, game.js:828-838) causes no grief, although a battlefield death does. The squad's break-off line (Temper.will) is computed at launch (sortie.js:234) and never shown; only a flavour line is logged after commitment (sortie.js:246-247).

REUSABLE PARTS ALREADY PRESENT. Field.withdraw and the portal logic that treats a withdrawn squad as finished (field.js:382-397, 1355, 1600-1607); Tactics.grieve and per-map resolve (tactics.js:425-466, field.js:569-596); the whole injury plumbing; Report.renderRun; Bonds.describe/relations; Temper.will/readParty. Every proposal below is built from these.

LIMITS OF THIS ANALYSIS. I did not use the browser. All harness numbers (test/field.harness.js copies in the scratchpad, 'on' variant, seeded, 10-30 runs per type) come from field.js's plain attrition resolver, so they are relative and not combat.js numbers. Real-combat behaviour of wounds, retreat and temper drift is unmeasured and needs a pass in the browser.

proposals.title: Replace the free 'Call it off' with a retreat order
proposals.problem: A player who watches a run can undo every death: abandon() frees the whole party and Roster.fall only runs at settlement, so a squad member marked down on the map is alive again after one click. Measured relative cost of doing this at the first death is about 6% of payouts. Every death-prevention feature (wormhole escape hatch, break-off, potions, tactics retreat) is worth little while a free undo exists, and the bonds, grief and memorial systems get no occasions.

sortie.js:450 Roster.fall is only reached from settle() (sortie.js:439), which is only called when s.result is set (sortie.js:387)

sortie.js:177, 181 and sortie.js:226-227 bestiary entries and aptitude xp are written to the real characters during the run and survive abandon
sortie.js:15-16 the file header states 'Death here is permanent'; sortie.js:983 UI text still says 'Leaving the page abandons a run in progress', although persist/resume (sortie.js:294-336) keeps it
field.js:1235-1249, 1251-1262 a death lands in kill() when the skirmish playback ends; the character stays on the roster until settle()

field.js:382-388 withdraw(); field.js:391-397 pullOut(); field.js:487 withdrawn squads get the exit goal; field.js:1355 portalTick treats s.withdrew as work done so the gate forms; field.js:1600-1607 verdict; field.js:1458-1462 callBack() is the existing player-to-field order

Node, plain-attrition harness, POW 0.6, 210 runs: 14.3% of runs have a death, 5.7 points of runs are won with a death, 27% of deaths are in won runs; POW 0.45: 28.1%, 6.2 points, 12%

Node, same harness: retreat ordered between fights when average squad HP < 70% (26 orders in 180 runs) gives deaths/run 0.30 to 0.27 and wins 77% to 73%; fields set by hand because withdraw is not exported; all 180 runs terminated
proposals.change:
1. field.js: add retreat(s) { if (!s || s.result || s.withdrew || s.escalated) return false; withdraw(s, 'called back'); return true; } and export it beside callBack. The squad then takes the existing path: exit goal, portal forms at the extraction point (gate mode needs 20 in-game s standing at it, MT.PORTAL.open), engaged members leave only when their skirmish ends (pullOut skips a.engaged), verdict ends the run as a loss with the existing 'could not get clear' bound (STRAGGLE 900 s).
2. sortie.js: add contacted() = run.encounters has an entry, or any non-structure hostile actor has found or spotted set (both are saved actor keys, field.js:1939-1943). Before contact the button stays 'Call it off' and behaves as today. After contact abandon() refuses and the button reads 'Order a retreat' and calls F.retreat(run.field); once s.withdrew is set the button is disabled and reads 'Retreating'.
3. settle() needs no change: falls, grief, bonds 'survived', Crew.completed, trial failure and salvage loot already run for a lost result (sortie.js:439-541). The result line shows why = 'called back' or 'called back, and could not get clear'.
4. UI note beside the button: 'takes effect when the current fight ends'. Correct sortie.js:983 text to describe persist/resume.
5. Standfast contracts open the portal where the squad stands (field.js:1381-1389), so a retreat there is almost immediate; if that proves too cheap, hold a retreat on standfast for MT.PORTAL.open seconds like a gate.
proposals.playerEffect: Sending a squad is a commitment again. The decision during a watch changes from 'click Call it off if someone falls' to 'order the squad out before the next group reaches them, accepting the contract is lost and that people already in the next fight are not saved'. The retreat is a trade in the harness (about 3 fewer deaths and 4 fewer wins per 100 runs), so it is neither dominant nor useless.
proposals.secondOrder: Escape features gain value: Chorokinetic wormhole and breakOff (field.js:989-1050), healing potions supplied by Outfit (outfit.js:27-33, 150-167), tactics 'a step back' (tactics.js PLAYS.retreat). Grief, memorial entries, team rapport loss (Crew.mourn) and the 'survived' bond event (bonds.js EVENTS) occur at the rate the sim produces them instead of near zero for an attentive player. Skip becomes an explicit acceptance of risk. Trials failed by retreat re-roll through the existing Quests.fail path (sortie.js:527-530). Pairs with loop-readout, which gives the player the information to time the order.
proposals.risks: Deaths per watched run rise from near zero to roughly the simulated rate (0.24-0.30 per run at POW 0.6, 0.50 at POW 0.45, plain resolver), which players who rely on abandon will read as a nerf; ship with loop-readout and loop-wounds so the player has information and so injury is a lower-stakes outcome than death. The order cannot save members already inside the open skirmish, because combat.js resolves the whole fight in advance (field.js:1217-1225); only the escape hatch can. Harness figures are from the attrition resolver and need confirming in the browser. Loss-of-contract payout means players may hesitate to order retreats on high-payout contracts, which is intended.

proposals.title: Sorties spend stamina and leave wounds, so the roster has to rotate
proposals.problem: A returning squad is as fresh as a squad that never left. Stamina is not spent, c.injured is never set, and regen heals a mauled squad fully within 40 real seconds. The best four characters can run contracts back to back with Skip, limited only by clicks, and the other roster members never leave town. The injury system exists in full and has no producer.
evidence: missions.js:265-266 the only assignment of c.injured, in the branch taken when Roster is undefined; game.html:520 loads roster.js, so the browser never takes it

Node plain-attrition harness, POW 0.6, 12 runs per type, 809 survivors: lowest HP fraction reached is below 0.6 for 14%, below 0.3 for 6%; rule injured = round(30 x clamp((0.6 - low)/0.6, 0, 1)) injures 14.2% of survivors, mean 12.6 ticks among injured, 1.8 ticks per survivor
proposals.change:
1. sortie.js resolve(): after each fight record the lowest HP fraction reached per squad actor, a.low = min(a.low ?? 1, a.fighter.hp / a.fighter.maxHp). Add 'low' to ACTOR_KEYS (field.js:1939-1943) so a resumed run keeps it. Use the low point, not end HP, because REGEN restores HP before the squad is home.
2. settle(), for each survivor c with actor a: Condition.spend(c, { staminaCost: 25 + m.level * 1.5, casts: a.fighter ? a.fighter.stats.casts : 0 }), the same expression as missions.js:259; and c.injured = max(c.injured, round(Missions.INJURY_TICKS x clamp((WOUND_FROM - a.low) / WOUND_FROM, 0, 1))) with WOUND_FROM = 0.6 (INJURY_TICKS is 30 ticks = 5 min, exported at missions.js:290).
3. Log one line per run, not per person: names of those injured with ticks and the low point, e.g. 'Bram is out for 14 ticks: dropped to 18% HP at Goblin Camp'. The same fact is shown in the loop-ledger report.
4. Party box on the board: add 'N recovering, first back in X min' (sum of c.injured x TICK_MS).
5. Calibration target: about 15% of survivors injured at the win rate the harness puts at 75% (POW 0.6). Confirm the low-point distribution in real combat by logging a.low for a session before fixing WOUND_FROM.
6. Optional second step: scale the per-tick decrement by Lodging.restFor (0.90-1.60, economy.js LODGINGS) so bed quality sets who is back first.
proposals.playerEffect: The decision after a sortie becomes who goes next: send the wounded A-team after waiting up to 5 minutes, send the bench now, or spend a healing potion earlier to avoid the wound. Bench characters acquire a use. Waiting time becomes planning time (who is back when, which trial is blocked).
proposals.secondOrder: Healing potions and healer classes lift the low point, so Outfit's potion supply and the alchemist trade reduce downtime and not only deaths. Lodging rest and the Sanctum/Manor tiers decide recovery speed once the optional step is added, so the Field starts to depend on the Town tab. Stamina spent lowers the next fight's starting pools (combat.js:83-88) and sends tired members to the rota, which already handles Condition.isSpent. Injured members sit at home with a -15 morale target (condition.js:146), which feeds Condition.moraleMult and town output. Trials stop appearing for injured characters (quests.js:136), which makes timing a trial a planning question. The Hone and Staffing screens already skip injured characters (crew.js:249, 475).
proposals.risks: More waiting for an active player: a four-person squad has about 0.57 injured members per sortie at the harness rate, mean 2 minutes, worst case 5. Quests.offers drops injured characters from the trial list (quests.js:136), so cards may appear and disappear; consider showing them greyed. The thresholds were set from the plain-attrition harness and must be rechecked against combat.js fights. Interaction with loop-retreat: a retreating squad takes more hits on the walk out, so wounds and falls become the price of retreating, which is intended.

proposals.title: Show the squad's break-off line, pair bonds and role mix before launch and during the run
proposals.problem: The numbers that decide whether a squad lives are computed at launch and hidden. Temper.will(party) sets the crew count and HP at which the squad stops working and heads home, and the temper reading is only logged after the player has committed. The party box shows name, stars, race and scouting. Choosing who goes together is therefore done by opening individual sheets and guessing.

sortie.js:1021-1025 party box header shows only the scouting tier; sortie.js:1043-1046 each card shows name, stars, race, scouting

proposals.change:
1. Pre-launch block in the party box (sortie.js renderBoard), computed from the picked characters with calls that already exist:
   a. 'Breaks off when N or fewer of M are standing, or when the average HP of those standing is under X%': N = ceil(M x will.broken.crew) - 1, X = round(100 x will.broken.hp); 'first to call it: <will.voice>' when voice is set.
   b. Temper.readParty(party): word and note, moved from the post-launch log to here.

   d. Role mix: counts from Outfit.roleOf ('1 frontline, 1 ranged, 1 caster, 1 support'); flag 'no support' when none.
   e. Existing scouting line and, for an active team, the cohesion line (Crew.cohesion) stay.
2. Live block in the run side panel (renderSide), next to the retreat button: standing / total, average HP of those standing, the current break line including resolve (crewLine = will.broken.crew x (1 - 0.45 x resolve), field.js:375), and for the nearest closing group Field.odds(ours, Tactics.closing(s), Field.frontage(s, ours)) labelled 'squad's read of the next fight'.
3. Words first, fractions on hover, to respect the existing choice not to print raw temper numbers (game.js:1188-1191): the line reports an effect of the squad, not any individual's axis.
proposals.playerEffect: Party selection becomes a comparison: swapping one member visibly moves the break line, the pair list and the role mix, so a bold, loyal squad that will stay until almost wiped can be chosen deliberately, or avoided on a contract where staying is fatal. During a run the player sees how close the squad is to its own retreat threshold and can decide to order one earlier.
proposals.secondOrder: Teams and bonds become choices with a visible payoff before launch, not only through the cohesion percentage. Temper words that today appear only on the sheet start to matter at the selection screen. It supplies the information loop-retreat needs: without the readout the retreat order is a guess. Recording the squad's reading in the loop-ledger report lets the player compare the line they saw with what happened.
proposals.risks: Showing the break line makes part of a hidden mechanic readable; it reveals an effect, not the five axes, and Temper.read already gives words, but it moves the game toward optimisation of squad temper. Field.odds is the plain-attrition estimate the squad itself uses, not the combat.js result, so the live odds line must be labelled as the squad's read and not as a forecast. Mood is a mean plus the loudest voice (temper.js VOICE 0.35), so changing one member can move the line non-intuitively; show it live as picks change to make that visible.

proposals.title: Persist an after-action report for every Field sortie, with cause of each fall and a per-type record
proposals.problem: The Field is the main content and leaves nothing behind. The log is in memory, 'Back to the board' discards it, and the only record is one game-log line. Per-fight blocks are already computed and then thrown away. A player who loses a squad cannot tell whether the cause was the ground, a boss, an under-rested squad or a missing healer, and the memorial says only the mission name.

1. combat.js encounter(): collect party-side deaths, deaths.push({ name: t.name, by: killer && killer.name, at: ctx.tick }) in the existing onDeath callback (combat.js:618), and return them with kills.
2. sortie.js: in resolve() store per fight the ground word and width (F.frontage, F.groundWord) and the squad's average HP fraction at fight start on run.fights[]. In settle() build one compact record and unshift it onto gs.field.history, capped at 20: { id, at, mission {name, icon, type, label, level, map, twists, trial?}, won, why, escalated, clock, party[{id, name, alive, low, dealt, taken, healed, casts, potions, kills}], fights[{n, won, timedOut, ticks, enemies[{name, level, alive}], ground, avgHpAtStart, downs}], deaths[{name, by, fight}], lines (non-indented log lines, last 40), paid, salvage }. Expected size about 2-3 KB per record.
3. Board: a collapsible 'Reports' box (collapsible() key 'reports', sortie.js:588) with one tab per record, rendered with Report.renderRun (pass mission as the name string, which hits the existing fallback) plus a short 'What decided it' block built only from record fields: the result why-string; the fight in which the first member fell, with enemies, ground width and squad HP at start; unused potions and whether any support role was present (Outfit.roleOf). 'Back to the board' opens the newest report first.
4. Roster.fall cause becomes '<mission>: <by>' when the killer is known; memorial cards (sortie.js:1096-1126) show it.
5. gs.field.types[type] = { sent, won, dead } updated in settle(); each contract card (missionCard, sortie.js:768) adds 'your record: 5 sent, 4 won, 1 person lost' when sent > 0. These are counts of things the player did, so they satisfy the traceability rule.
proposals.playerEffect: After a loss the player can read what happened and change one thing: bring support, avoid open ground, wait for wounds to clear. After a win they can see who carried it. Contract choice gets an evidence base: the cards report how this town has actually fared at each type, which replaces guessing from a payout multiplier that does not follow risk.
proposals.secondOrder: Feeds loop-record (per-character counters are filled from the same settle() pass) and gives loop-wounds and loop-retreat a place to explain themselves ('dropped to 18% HP', 'called back'). The bestiary tiers (kills needed to learn weaknesses) become something the player can read in context: a report row can say 'weakness unknown, 2 kills of 5 needed'. The memorial gains a cause. The per-type record gives the contract board a feedback loop without changing payouts.
proposals.risks: State size: 20 records at 2-3 KB is about 50 KB in localStorage next to a save that already holds every character; measure save size before and after. The 'what decided it' block must derive from recorded facts only; avoid free-text inference that can be wrong. Report.renderRun reads Bestiary.knowledge per enemy, so unknown species stay masked correctly; check that a record outlives a species being renamed. Risk and reward mismatch in the harness table is a relative result from the attrition resolver and does not justify retuning payouts by itself; the per-type record is the safer response.

proposals.title: Give each character a service record, keep it on the memorial, and make the altar read it
proposals.problem: A character is a stat block with a face. Nothing accumulates about what they did, so there is no reason to prefer one 3-star swordsman over another beyond numbers, and a death leaves a name, a cause and top aptitudes. Bonds, which are the strongest attachment data in the game, are deleted at death. Sacrificing a character at the altar costs the survivors nothing, although a battlefield death does.
evidence: grep over *.js: no c.record, c.service, c.deeds or equivalent field exists; bonds.js:115 p.runs is the only per-pair history
roster.js:95-105 memorial entry: uuid, face, id, name, race, bodyType, stars, cause, at, served, selections, top four aptitudes

proposals.change:
1. Data, on the character, plain JSON, defaulted in game.js load(): c.record = { out, won, kills, witnessed, closeCall: { low, mission, at } | null, last: { mission, won, at } | null }. All counters, no stored labels.
2. Writers, all in sortie.js: resolve() adds credited kills (killer.char); settle() increments out for each survivor, won when the contract completed, witnessed by the number of squad members who fell on a map they were on, closeCall when a.low is the lowest seen, last always.
3. Roster.fall (roster.js:87) copies c.record and the two strongest bonds with v above 12 (name, Bonds.tier word, runs), taken before Bonds.mourn deletes them. Bonds is resolved optionally like the other modules. Memorial cards show: record counts, closest two, cause with killer (from loop-ledger).
4. Sheet: a 'Record' section after Company: sorties, wins, kills, comrades lost, closest call with mission and time, last sortie. Party picker cards (sortie.js:1043) add 'N sorties, last: won' and the injured mark. Names are readings only: an optional word ('new' under 3 sorties, 'seasoned' from 8, 'veteran' from 20) computed in one function and used by display code alone.
5. Altar: expose Bonds.grief(state, c, chars) as a pure version of mourn's first half (relations with v above 12, hit = min(35, v x GRIEF)). Each offering row lists who would grieve and the morale hit; the confirmation line names the record ('14 sorties, 31 kills'). sacrificeTo calls grieve(sac) after Sacrifice.apply, so the existing log lines, morale hits and Crew.mourn happen as for a battlefield death.
proposals.playerEffect: Characters differ by what they have been through, visible at the three places the player makes a decision about a person: the party picker, the altar and the memorial. The altar, which is currently the free disposal path for the 45% of pulls that are 1-star, becomes a choice with named consequences, and a well-liked character can be kept out of it because the cost is shown.
proposals.secondOrder: Altar offerings now depend on bonds and on the sortie history, which couples the Altar tab to the Field. Tactics already reads pair runs (tactics.js:101-115); the record gives the picker a way to build squads from people who have worked together. Grief after a sacrifice feeds Condition morale and Crew.mourn, which already exist. proposals.playerEffect: A character who comes back from the worst map of the season is described differently on the sheet afterwards, and the squad that includes them may leave a fight at a different point. proposals.title: One strength reading for both sides of the field, taken from the fighter
proposals.problem: Stand, hold, pounce, retreat, and the hostile decision to collect allies before closing all come from Field.odds (power x health). In the browser game every squad member has power 4 and speed 0.55 whatever their stars, class, gear or DEX, and hostile power is a five-row grade table that does not read the mission level (a level-10 rat has 1.9x the HP and 1.9x the damage of a level-3 rat, both power 1). The reading saturates: 0.53 to 0.96 over 54 test cases, while the combat model's win rate for the same cases runs from 0 to 100%. With the inputs the browser game produces, the field plays do not fire: 0.00 details and 0.00 stands per run over extermination, raid, hold, survival and escort (8 runs each), against 2.05 and 1.85 per run with the inputs the balance harness invents. The harness therefore tunes tactics against a situation the game never produces.
evidence: field.js:2059 `power: c.power || 4, speed: BASE_SPEED * (c.speed || 1)`; no code outside the harness sets c.power or c.speed (grep). Node: 1-star and 5-star Fighter both give power 4, speed 0.55.
sortie.js:149-150 fighterFor copies only maxHp and hp from the real fighter back to the actor.

field.js:80-81 and 1679-1680: hostile power and pre-fight HP come from GRADE_POWER / GRADE_HP by grade (and mark/swarm factors); level is not an input. Node (scales.js): forest_rat level 3 hp 125 dmg 13.6, level 10 hp 235 dmg 26.2, same power 1 and hp 20 in the field.

field.js:1106-1115 odds(); tactics.js:154 judge() reads it; tactics.js:273-276, 300, 322 gate every play on `oddsHere < ok` (GOOD 0.6, tactics.js:135) or `< HOPELESS` (0.35, tactics.js:132); field.js:825 hostile rally needs odds < RALLY_AT 0.45.

stats.js:49 walkSpeed has no reader; field.js:1691 speedOf gives hostiles dex-based legs; field.js:989-1000 escapeHatch comment says the on-foot break-off is 'a question about legs (speedOf)' but squad legs are all equal.
test/field.harness.js:38 invents c.maxHp, c.power and c.speed per character (power = 3 + stars x 0.7 + (STR+DEX)/20, times POW), so harness results describe different inputs from the game.

Node odds_vs_truth3.js (4-fighter gearless squads, classes fighter/ranger/barbarian/rogue, 3 mission levels x 3 star tiers x 6 packs, 16 combat.js encounters each): reading vs win rate Spearman 0.34. Example: level 3 vs 6 goblins, 1-star squad reading 0.94 and win 0%, 5-star squad reading 0.96 and win 100%; level 14 vs 6 goblins, 5-star reading 0.96, win 0%.

Same script: a rating from the fighter's own base block, offense = max(damage, magicDamage) x speed/BAR x (1 + crit x (critDamage - 1)), health = maxHp x (1 + armor/10), odds = (sum offense x sum health) ratio, gives Spearman 0.83 against the same win rates. Rows with win rate between 0.2 and 0.8 sit at plain-ratio odds 0.14-0.39 (median about 0.3), so the squad side needs a calibration factor of about 2.3.
proposals.change: 1) combat.js: add rating(f) returning { power, guard } from f.base using the expression above (power in damage per second at 10 ticks per second; guard = maxHp x (1 + armor/10)). Export it beside fromMonster. 2) sortie.js fighterFor: after the cohesion multiplier (sortie.js:126-131) set a.power = RATE_K x rating(fighter).power and a.guard = rating(fighter).guard; set a.speed = BASE_SPEED x derived.walkSpeed / 4 (walkSpeed at DEX 10 is 4.0, which puts it on the same scale as speedOf's 0.7 + dex/30 = 1.03). 3) Hostiles: sortie.js supplies rateFoe(species, level) = rating(Combat.fromMonster(def, level, {}, {})) cached per species and level; field.js makeActor uses it for power and starting HP when present and falls back to GRADE_POWER / GRADE_HP otherwise (tests, bare parties). Level comes from the same expression sortie.fighterFor uses (mission level + GRADE_BUMP + levelOffset). 4) field.js fightHp multiplies a.hp by a.guard (default 1). 5) New test/rating.harness.js fits RATE_K so odds 0.5 coincides with a 0.5 win rate in Combat.encounter, over a grid that includes casters, healers and geared squads; commit the fitted value. 6) field.harness.js passes the same rate hook instead of inventing power, speed and maxHp; re-run at POW 0.6 and 0.45 and refit GOOD/HOPELESS/RALLY_AT only if the stand and retreat counts fall outside the current ranges.
proposals.playerEffect: Who is in the squad and what they carry changes how the squad behaves on the map, and the log says so. A strong squad takes a fight where it stands; the same pack read by a weak squad produces 'they fall back and stand in a doorway' or 'they read it and go' lines before anyone is hurt. Hostile groups collect allies when the squad is strong enough to need it. A retreat decision that fires before a fight is the cheapest death prevention in the game, and today it cannot fire against anything below legendary grade.
proposals.secondOrder: Smithy output, class, stars and sacrifices now change tactics, not only fight results, because Stats.effective already feeds fromCharacter. DEX gets a second job: a squad with a slow member strings out on the map (the harness already runs mixed speeds through c.speed), and the on-foot break-off in escapeHatch depends on real legs against speedOf. The systems-will-axis and systems-meal-buffs proposals feed this automatically because the rating reads the fighter after their modifiers. Cohesion bonus order matters: the rating must be read after sortie.js:126-131 applies it.
proposals.risks: GOOD, HOPELESS, EDGE and RALLY_AT were tuned on harness values; the new distribution of readings will change how often each play fires, so expect one tuning pass. My measurement used gearless squads of four melee classes, so healers, casters and the effect of gear on the fit are not measured; the calibration step must include them (a healer's value is not in max(damage, magicDamage)). Squads with mixed speeds string out and meet fights piecemeal, which is more dangerous for the slow member. Armor is a flat per-hit subtraction in Elements.slice, so (1 + armor/10) is an approximation; a variant that models it against the opposing mean hit scored 0.84 against 0.83, so the simple form is adequate.

proposals.title: One mission debrief for the Gate and the Field, and one death path
proposals.problem: Contracts on the Field tab end through Sortie.settle, which skips four hooks that zone runs on the Gate tab get from Missions.finish. Class XP is never earned on a contract; the 'loot x1.1 ... x1.35' on eight classes (Thief x1.35, Spy x1.15) pays nothing on a contract; nobody spends stamina or caster mana on a contract, so condition.js's stated purpose (rest before a mission matters) does not apply to the main mission format; Classes.fought exists and nothing calls it. The reverse gaps exist too: Gate runs forge no bonds and cause no grief. Deaths enter by three routes and only the Field route grieves: a character sacrificed at the altar costs their friends no morale, and Bonds.tidy is never called.

For each survivor: Classes.returned(c, {won}) plus Classes.fought(c, encounters); Condition.spend(c, { staminaCost, casts }) where casts is fighter.stats.casts and staminaCost is DRAIN.gather x clockTicks for a field run (same table as a work shift) and the existing flat formula for a Gate run; Condition.outcome (moved out of both callers); Bonds.together events for both formats. proposals.playerEffect: A contract now costs the squad what a zone run costs. Casters come home with an empty pool and need about 50 resting ticks (POOL_REGEN 2% per tick) before the next sortie, so the kitchen, bed quality and a second squad become part of running contracts. Class ranks and specialisations progress from field work, including for the character on a star trial. The Thief's x1.35 and the other seven loot classes affect pay and the log says by how much. Sacrificing a close friend's bonded partner costs the friend morale, as a battlefield death does.
proposals.secondOrder: Condition's party-picker inputs become decisions (see systems-will-axis for showing them). Class specialise() triggers can fire from contract work. Offline catch-up (MAX_OFFLINE_TICKS 2880) restores all pools, so the cost only bites during active play. The Gate gains bond formation and grief, which makes party composition there matter too. Quests.pass is unchanged.

Stamina cost of 68 on a 110 tank puts every member in the tired band after each contract; with REST_BASE 4 + 0.2 x CON per tick it recovers in about 11 ticks, so the cost is mild and mana is the real constraint. The loot multiplier raises contract pay by up to 35% for a Thief party; if that is too much, cap it or apply it to the resource payout only. sortie.js and missions.js are touched by systems-wounds, systems-will-axis and systems-cohesion-from-pairs, so this one should land first or share an owner.

proposals.title: Carry wounds home through the existing injured counter, healed by bed and food
proposals.problem: Every sortie starts at full HP and a survivor at 5% HP loses nothing afterwards, so the only cost of risk is death. c.injured, the counter that already blocks launching (sortie.js:206), crew staffing (crew.js:249, 475), morale (condition.js:146, temper.js:259), where the character walks (townlife.js:53), the token ring (townview.js:131) and the sheet text 'recovering (N ticks)' (game.js:993, 1180, 1387), is set only by a Node-only fallback (missions.js:265-266). In the browser all of that code is unreachable. Survivors do end hurt: across 588 survivors of seven combat.js matchups (single fights) the median end HP was 85%, 20% were under 60% and 8% under 30%, and HP accumulates over the several fights of one map.
evidence: combat.js:72 `hp: d.hp, maxHp: d.hp` on every fighter build, so nothing from the last mission carries over.

missions.js:265-266 `if (typeof Roster !== 'undefined') { Roster.fall(...) } else c.injured = INJURY_TICKS`; Roster is always loaded in the browser, so injured is never set there. missions.js:167 decrements it one per tick for everyone.

Depends on a hook in settle; trivial to add without systems-one-debrief.

proposals.title: One willingness axis: morale seeds resolve, and the squad's will sets the line for leaving a fight
proposals.problem: temper.js:320 says the squad's bear line is where a temper is worth somebody's life, but that line is applied only between fights (field.js:362-381, 2108). A fight is resolved inside Combat.encounter, and the only way out of it is escapeHatch, which uses fixed constants (field.js:903-904, 1013), so a craven squad and a fearless one leave a losing fight at the same HP. Separately, morale and stamina never reach the field (condition.js:26), and resolve, the existing -1..+1 'willingness to be here' that combat.js and broken() both read, starts at 0 for everyone and moves only on a death. Lodging, food, rest and bonds therefore cannot change how a squad behaves in the dungeon. The party picker also shows neither morale nor stamina (sortie.js:1043-1045).
evidence: field.js:903-904 ESCAPE_HP 0.4, ESCAPE_LOW 0.2 and field.js:1013 `bad = (down > 0 && avg < 0.7) || avg < ESCAPE_HP || (lowest < ESCAPE_LOW && foeAvg > 0.4)`: no reference to willOf(s) or resolveOf(s) inside escapeHatch (field.js:989-1020).
field.js:362-381 broken() scales its lines by willOf(s).broken and `1 - 0.45 x resolveOf(s)`; temper.js:338-352 will() builds broken.hp = clamp(0.25 x scale, 0.06, 0.6) from the squad's mood.
field.js:580-585 grieved() is the only writer of a.resolve; sortie.js:167 passes `a.resolve || 0` to the fighter; combat.js:393-411 uses it for action values and the fear line.

condition.js moraleTarget (lines 128-152) already sums bed, food, rest, bonds and temper into a 0-100 morale; game.js:408 ticks it; the only consumers are moraleMult for town output (condition.js:58) and the facet registry.

By squad nerve+grit tercile: timid squads deaths per run 0.647 -> 0.578 and wins 59.0% -> 54.2%; middle 0.514 -> 0.530 and 65.7% -> 65.3%; bold 0.508 -> 0.568 and 60.8% -> 62.0%. Aggregate deaths 0.556 -> 0.559, wins 61.9% -> 60.5%.
proposals.change: 1) field.js escapeHatch: lean = clamp((willOf(s).broken.hp / BROKEN_HP) x (1 - 0.45 x resolveOf(s)), 0.4, 2.0); multiply the 0.7 (cap 0.95), ESCAPE_HP (cap 0.75) and ESCAPE_LOW (cap 0.45) by it. Add the figure to the break-off log line ('breaks off below 33% average HP'). 2) condition.js: resolveSeed(c) = clamp((morale - 60) / 100, -0.4, 0.25) - (isSpent ? 0.15 : 0). Field.start (or sortie.launch after F.start) sets a.resolve to it for each squad actor; the existing floor mechanism is untouched. 3) sortie.js picker cards add stamina and morale band labels (Condition.describe) and the selected party line adds Temper.readParty plus the leave line for the party's will, so the figures that feed the seed are visible before launch. The launch log prints each member's seed.
proposals.playerEffect: Who goes together matters in the fight, not only on the map. A rested, well-housed squad starts steady and stays in fights longer; a squad whose last contract failed (morale -12, -6 per death) starts shaken and leaves earlier. A cunning or timid squad becomes the safe choice for a contract where survival matters, and a bold one the choice where finishing matters. Measured: about 10% fewer deaths per run for timid squads and 12% more for bold ones, with the aggregate unchanged.
proposals.secondOrder: Lodging morale (-18 to +22), bonds company (+/-14), the kitchen (+6 fed, FED_ROUGH) and injury (-15) now reach permadeath through resolve. Grief floors and panic keep working because they write the same variable. Combat action values (attack x1.28 at +1, heal x0.78) shift with morale, so a steady squad heals less and attacks more. Morale loops: a win gives +8, so success compounds slightly and failure compounds in the other direction; the clamp keeps the seed within -0.4..+0.25.
proposals.risks: The direction of the high-morale side is a choice: positive resolve keeps a squad in fights longer, which in permadeath terms is more risk, and the bold-tercile result (+12% deaths) shows it. proposals.playerEffect: Feeding the squad before a contract becomes an action with a visible result: a character who rested while a Fine stew was in the pantry goes out with +1 STR and +2 CON for the sortie, and the sheet says why. The kitchen tier unlock list (porridge to banquet), the cook's aptitude and the farm output all convert into combat numbers. Running out of meals has a cost on a specific character (no FED_REST), not on a boolean for the whole town.
proposals.secondOrder: Crew.demands already sizes farms and the kitchen from the roster's eating rate (crew.js:287-300), so the supply chain is unchanged and gains a reason to exceed the minimum. The systems-field-rating proposal reads the fighter after the buff, so meals change tactics as well as damage. FED_REST now says which characters recover faster.

The buff also lifts town output through effective(), which could inflate the economy unless the duration stays short. Per-character eating changes the pantry draw from a count to a sum over characters; the rate is the same (0.02 per resting tick) but best-first selection drains high-quality meals faster than the current worst-first rule. effCache is keyed on base+bonus, so any other code that mutates c.cond.meal outside Condition would bypass invalidation.

proposals.title: Cohesion computed from the party that actually goes, using the bond ledger
proposals.problem: The team bonus (up to +18% damage and +9% armour) belongs to a saved Team record and not to the people on the sortie. sortie.launch grants it only if every member going is on the active team, then scores the whole team including members who stayed home. proposals.secondOrder: Bonds events other than 'mission' (shift 0.06, lodging 0.15) still move pair value and accord but not runs, so only walking out together builds rapport, as designed. proposals.secondOrder: Making the aptitude ceiling explicit surfaces the existing disagreement between prowess (S**) and class fit (A+): both stay as they are in this change, and the overseer can decide later whether Might/Guard radar axes should use the advance cap. verdicts.attack: The order cannot change the fight the player is watching: combat.js resolves the whole skirmish when it opens (field.js:1217-1225) and deaths land when the playback ends (field.js:1242), so after the first '⚔️ meet' line the button only decides whether the squad walks out before the NEXT group arrives. The real lever is pre-contact, where 'Call it off' already exists and stays free. After contact the proposal also removes the only exit from a stalled run until STRAGGLE (900 in-game s, field.js:1606) ends it. A retreat-every-time player loses only the contract and a trial reroll, but that is the intended price and it already costs more than abandon does today (Condition.outcome -12 at condition.js:196, Quests.fail at sortie.js:528), so this is not a disguised nerf.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: abandon() sortie.js:338-350 clears c.mission with no alive check and no Roster.fall; Roster.fall only at sortie.js:450 inside settle(), reached only when s.result is set (sortie.js:387); kill() marks the actor only (field.js:1251-1268); withdraw/pullOut field.js:382-397; portalTick treats s.withdrew as done (field.js:1355); verdict ends a withdrawn run (field.js:1600-1607); FieldAPI exports callBack and not withdraw (field.js:2139-2141); persist/resume keep a run across reloads so only the button undoes a death. My harness run at POW 0.6 (420 runs) reproduces 77% wins and 0.28-0.30 deaths/run. The '6% of payouts' figure is from the plain attrition resolver and is relative only.
verdicts.demand: Keep 'Call it off' before contact exactly as today. After contact the retreat must end through settle() as a loss with no new settlement path. Ship the live standing/total and average-HP block from loop-readout in the same change, or the order is a blind guess. Confirm s.withdrew and s.phase survive Field.save/restore (field.js:1975-2025) so the button state is right after a reload. Verify in the browser, not the harness, that a squad under retreat on a gate contract actually reaches the portal within STRAGGLE on the three largest maps.

verdicts.attack: It is a cooldown dressed as a decision: with Skip a sortie takes seconds, so 'who goes next' is a 2-5 minute wait or a bench pick, and a roster with eight idle 3-stars never feels it. The low-point rule ignores healing after the dip, so a Cleric who brought someone back from 15% still sends them to bed, which contradicts the claim that healers reduce downtime. The stamina term (25 + 1.5 x level) is about 1.5 minutes of rest at condition.js:168, i.e. nothing.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: c.injured has no browser writer (missions.js:265-266 is the Roster-undefined branch; game.js:93 only defaults it to 0) and readers at sortie.js:206, 1018; crew.js:249, 475; condition.js:146, 151; quests.js:136, 155; game.js:651, 664, 1180; townlife.js:53, 62. missions.js:167 decrements it every town tick via game.js:470. The 14% injured rate and the low-point distribution come from the attrition resolver and are unverified in combat.js.

The picker shows recovering characters greyed with the tick count and the low point that caused it, instead of omitting them. Calibrate WOUND_FROM from a.low logged in real combat.js fights over one session, and state the resulting share of sorties that leave at least one member unavailable.

verdicts.attack: Item 1a prints a derived number ('breaks off when 2 or fewer of 4 are standing') that the player cannot trace to anything they can click: it is five hidden axes through temper.js:338-343, which fails numbers-must-be-traceable and undoes the decision at game.js:1188-1191 to keep temper out of the UI as numbers (the hover fraction is the number). Item 2's 'squad's read of the next fight' is Field.odds, which systems-field-rating shows is nearly uncorrelated with real outcomes because every squad member has power 4 (field.js:2059); printing it teaches the player to trust a wrong figure.

verdicts.attack: It is reading material, not a mechanic: a player who Skips every run may never open it, and the 'What decided it' block is one sentence away from telling the player something false. Cap at 10 records and report save size before and after. Killer names resolve through Bestiary.knowledge so an unmet species stays masked. The veteran word is computed from the counts in one display function and read by no behaviour. Old saves start at zero and the sheet says so. verdicts.attack: The builder's own harness shows no measurable change at +/-15 on every axis (wins 77-78%, deaths 0.27-0.30, within noise), so the mechanic is inert and what ships is a sheet line plus two new persistent fields (temperBorn, arc) and a positive feedback loop: hardened characters take more risk, see more deaths, harden further. Temper is 'who somebody is when nobody is giving orders' (temper.js:1-44), rolled once, with names as readings; drifting the axes adds an eleventh writer of state for an effect a player cannot see within a session (bands are 20 wide, the cap is 18, so at most one band flips). The expressive content ('saw Bram fall at Goblin Camp') is already delivered by loop-record's witnessed and closeCall counters without touching the axes, and loop-retreat plus loop-readout make the existing per-map resolve visible and consequential.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: temper.js:154-160 ensure() is the only axis writer (grep); tactics.js:425-475 reaction/grieve; field.js:571-591 writes a.resolve with a floor; ACTOR_KEYS carries resolve and floor (field.js:1939-1943); settle() copies nothing back (sortie.js:439-541); ai.js:188-193 signature includes temper; band edges at temper.js:51-100. verdicts.attack: It swaps one magic table for a fitted constant (RATE_K about 2.3) and makes the field's judgement depend on combat.js, so the committed harness (plain resolver, invented power) stops describing the game unless it is switched to the same hook, and every tactics threshold (GOOD 0.6, HOPELESS 0.35, EDGE 0.05, RALLY_AT 0.45) was tuned on the old distribution. Per-member speed from walkSpeed strings squads out and gets the slow member killed under permadeath, which is the opposite of what the user values.

Clamp squad speed to 0.9-1.1 of BASE_SPEED in the first pass. Switch test/field.harness.js to the same rating hook and report stands/details per run before and after on the committed harness, with any GOOD/HOPELESS/RALLY_AT retune shown as numbers and the aggregate deaths/run not rising.

verdicts.attack: Class XP per contract at XP.mission 1.5 flat (classes.js:60, 1581) with several contracts an hour outruns the rank tuning; the Thief's x1.35 on contracts is a straight pay rise on the main income source; the stamina term (about 68) recovers in 11 ticks so it is noise, and the mana term is a second rate limiter on casters on top of loop-wounds. Gate runs gaining bonds and grief changes a mode nobody asked about.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: missions.js:256 Classes.returned, 258-260 Condition.spend/outcome, 265 Roster.fall, 271 partyLoot; sortie.js settle() (439-541) calls only Condition.outcome at 517; worth at sortie.js:479 has no loot term; classes.js:1579-1581 and grep: fought() has no caller; combat.js:83-88 reads the pools; game.js:493 Gate deaths call Crew.mourn only; sacrifice.js:181 and game.js:828-838 call neither grieve nor Bonds.mourn; Bonds.tidy (bonds.js:251) has no caller; MT.TIME.stepMs 200 at missiontypes.js:43-47.

Class XP scaled by encounters through Classes.fought with returned() reduced so a contract is worth about one Gate run. The loot multiplier applied to the resource payout or capped at x1.15 on contracts until measured. The single death entry in game.js becomes the only browser caller of Roster.fall. Gate cohesion stays with systems-cohesion-from-pairs.

verdicts.attack: The trigger does not fire in the real game: settle() runs after the walk home and REGEN (sortie.js:23, 370-378) restores 0.5% of max HP per in-game second out of a fight, so a survivor is full 200 in-game seconds (40 real seconds at 1x) after the last fight and 'lost = 1 - hp/maxHp >= 0.15' is almost never true. The 588-survivor sample is single combat.js encounters with no walk and no REGEN, which is not what settle() sees. WOUND_TICKS 120 (8 minutes for a 40% loss) is a guess against an idle player.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: combat.js:72 builds hp from derived each time; missions.js:165-167 and the readers as listed; lodging.js:178-181 restFor (0.90 tent to 1.60 sanctum, 0.75 roofless); condition.js:49 FED_REST 1.25; endhp.js in the scratchpad runs Combat.encounter with frontage 8 and no field regen, so its p50 0.85 end HP is a per-fight figure, not a per-sortie one.

verdicts.attack: Item 2 makes a well-housed, fed, rested squad stay in losing fights longer (bold tercile +12% deaths in the builder's own bucket run), so the town investments the game asks for raise the death rate under permadeath. The aggregate is flat (0.556 to 0.559 deaths/run), so it moves risk between squads rather than creating a decision the player can win. Item 1 is a one-line wiring of an existing axis into an existing mechanism and is the only part with a clear direction; item 3 is needed anyway by loop-wounds and systems-one-debrief.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: escapeHatch field.js:989-1020 uses fixed ESCAPE_HP/ESCAPE_LOW (903-904, 1013) with no willOf/resolveOf; broken() uses both (362-380); grieved() is the only writer of a.resolve (571-591); moraleTarget condition.js:133-153; combat.js:393-394 scales action values by resolve; sortie.js:1043-1045 shows no morale or stamina. sim/test/bucket.js is the stock harness with Temper.mood recorded per run; its aggregate 0.556 deaths/run matches my POW 0.45 run (0.54-0.55).

Seed resolve from the negative side only (morale under 60 or isSpent) so lodging and food never raise deaths; show one bucket run where no tercile's deaths/run rises. Picker rendering shares an owner with loop-readout.

verdicts.attack: The builder's own cells show +2 on all six stats taking a 33% win to 80% and a Masterwork banquet (+4 x 6) to 93%, so an eaten meal outweighs four Masterwork weapons and the split rule is a patch on top. Routing the buff through Stats.effective lifts town output, scouting, honing and class fitness (every reader of effective()), with effCache keyed on base+bonus so any writer outside Condition bypasses invalidation. The player's decision is indirect: meals are eaten automatically by whoever rests, so the choice is still kitchen tier and cook, which exist already.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: economy.js:191-197 MEALS and 214-218 buffs rolled from quality; game.js:1898 is the only reader of meal buffs (combat.js .buffs are fighter buffs); pooled eating at game.js:396-400 and eatMeals worst-first at 549-559; stats.js:134-141 equipBonus and 154-162 cache. buff_size.js in the scratchpad is a 40-encounter grid carrying the bonus in a fake charm slot, gearless, so the win-rate deltas are plausible but not geared.
verdicts.demand: Either implement with the buff applied in Combat.fromCharacter only, not Stats.effective, capped so a Masterwork banquet moves the harness win rate by at most 10 points, eaten per character at departure from the best meal in the pantry; or delete the buffs field and the inventory label as a cleanup. Do not change the pantry draw to per-character hunger accrual in the same step as the buff.

revised.stateOfGame:
LOOP AS CODED. Summon costs 100 gems, has no roster cap (game.js:754-788) and shows one card that the next pull replaces (game.js:2659-2666). Town staffing is automated: 'Optimal jobs' (game.js:1710), the rota (game.js:637-681) and 'Hone' (game.js:1699) leave a few clicks per hour. There are two mission systems. The Gate (14 fixed zones, missions.js:75-90) resolves on town ticks with no input after launch, writes state.missions.done (missions.js:276), and has a debrief (game.js:2346-2360). The Field (sortie.js, 16 contract types) runs live on a map, and its contract level is read from the Gate's clears (sortie.js:42-50). The Field player decides which of 5 contracts (board rolls every 6 min, or at once through a free 'Ask around' button, sortie.js:22, 1006-1011) and which party. During a run the only controls are speed, camera, Skip, 'Fall back' (defence contracts only) and 'Call it off' (sortie.js:1264-1271). Advancement trials (quests.js) and the altar (game.js:2411) are the two other sinks for characters.

SCARCITY. Gems are not the constraint. Measured in Node: mean maintenance output is 1.22 gems/tick per character before rest, morale and temper factors (4000 sampled pulls), which is about 4.9 gems/min per worker at the 2/3 duty cycle (game.js:513-514). A level-3 contract averages 228 gems (40 rolls per type through MT.roll, payout formula sortie.js:479) over 3.05 min of real time at 1x, about 75 gems/min for the party, versus about 20 gems/min for the same four on maintenance. Skip (sortie.js:404-414) plus the free reroll make that ratio limited only by clicks. The scarce things are therefore people and attention, which makes consequences to people the main lever on engagement.

WHAT A SORTIE COSTS THE PEOPLE ON IT. Survivors pay nothing: sortie.js settle() (439-541) never calls Condition.spend (the Gate does, missions.js:259) and never sets c.injured. c.injured has about 15 consumers (party pickers, rota, trials, morale, town map, roster tile) and no producer in the browser: its only writer, missions.js:266, sits in the branch for Roster being undefined, and roster.js is loaded (game.html:520). Death is also optional: 'Call it off' (sortie.js:338-350) frees the whole party without checking who is down, while Roster.fall runs only inside settle() (sortie.js:450). Aptitude xp and bestiary entries earned during the run are kept (sortie.js:177, 181). In the plain-attrition harness at POW 0.6, 14.3% of runs contain a death and only 5.7 points of runs are both won and contain a death, so abandoning at the first death keeps every life and costs about 6% of payouts.

WHAT THE PLAYER CANNOT SEE OR KEEP. The Field has no debrief. Bestiary.record already builds per-fight encounter blocks on the run object (bestiary.js:95-106), but persist() omits them (sortie.js:299-302), 'Back to the board' discards the run (sortie.js:1281) and Report.renderRun is only called for Gate runs. A character has no history: no c.record field exists, the memorial stores name, stars, cause, time served and top aptitudes (roster.js:95-105), and Bonds.mourn deletes the dead's bonds (bonds.js:240-246) after at most four log lines (game.js:384). Temper axes are written once at roll (temper.js:154-160; no other writer). Sacrifice (sacrifice.js:177-181, game.js:828-838) causes no grief, although a battlefield death does. The squad's break-off line (Temper.will) is computed at launch (sortie.js:234) and never shown; only a flavour line is logged after commitment (sortie.js:246-247).

REUSABLE PARTS ALREADY PRESENT. Field.withdraw and the portal logic that treats a withdrawn squad as finished (field.js:382-397, 1355, 1600-1607); Tactics.grieve and per-map resolve (tactics.js:425-466, field.js:569-596); the whole injury plumbing; Report.renderRun; Bonds.describe/relations; Temper.will/readParty. Every proposal below is built from these.

LIMITS OF THIS ANALYSIS. I did not use the browser. All harness numbers (test/field.harness.js copies in the scratchpad, 'on' variant, seeded, 10-30 runs per type) come from field.js's plain attrition resolver, so they are relative and not combat.js numbers. Real-combat behaviour of wounds, retreat and temper drift is unmeasured and needs a pass in the browser.

proposals.problem: abandon() frees the whole party and Roster.fall only runs at settlement, so a squad member who fell on the map is alive again after one click. Measured on combat.js (not the attrition resolver): 147 of 900 sorties had a death, 52 of 631 won sorties (8.2%) had at least one, and 268 deaths in total, 67 of them in won sorties. A player who presses 'Call it off' at the first fall keeps all of those people and forgoes 8.2% of wins (counted by sortie, not payout-weighted). Every death-prevention feature (wormhole escape hatch, break-off, potions, tactics retreat) and every death-consequence system (grief, memorial, bonds 'survived', Crew.mourn) is worth little while this free undo exists.

proposals.title: Keep a run's team bonus across a reload, build fighters before changing state at launch, and stop a live run on Reset
proposals.problem: Four lifecycle faults around a sortie, found by the antagonists and checked against the code. (2) launch() pays a trial fee and sets c.mission before building fighters, and fighter construction can throw, which leaves the party flagged as out and a run object with no timer. (3) Reset replaces the game state while a sortie keeps ticking against the old state object. (4) Abandoning a trial before contact keeps the fee spent and the trial open, so relaunching pays twice.
evidence: sortie.js:299-302 persist() writes { id, party, loot, zone, started, state } only; sortie.js:312-336 resume() spreads that into run; sortie.js:258 launch() builds teamId, teamName and bonus into run; sortie.js:60-70 fighterFor reads run.bonus; sortie.js:511 settle() runs Crew.completed only when run.teamId is set; sortie.js:1272-1274 the run panel prints the team tag from run.teamName

2. launch(): reorder so every step that can throw precedes every step that changes state. After F.start and the run object are assembled, build all squad fighters inside a try/catch; on failure set run = null and return `${name} cannot be prepared: ${message}`. Move the trial payment (Quests.begin, sortie.js:215) and the c.mission assignment (sortie.js:263) after that block.
3. spellcraft.js randomSentence(): `if (!usable.length) return [];` after the usable filter (one line; root cause). buildGrimoire already skips specs that fail checkSentence. A character with no usable word then has an empty grimoire and still fights with a martial plan.

5. Sortie.discard(): stop the timer, forget(), run = null, no settle; called from the Reset handler (game.js:2679) before state is replaced. Export it in window.Sortie.

Reset no longer leaves a sortie running against a discarded save. Calling off a trial before contact returns the fee.

Refunding a trial fee changes the trial economy slightly: pre-contact abandon becomes free for trials as for contracts, which matches the intent of the free window. The spellcraft guard changes behaviour only where the code threw before. Rare trigger for the launch fault (1 in 1313 Alchemists through the UI path); the persist fault is certain on every reload with a team.
proposals.response: New proposal taken from the antagonists' 'missed' lists (the launch crash, persist omitting teamId and bonus, Reset with a live run, abandon after a trial). Both antagonists ranked the crash above every proposal; checked: it reproduces, and the root cause is one missing guard, but through the normal training path it is rare (1 in 1313 eligible Alchemists, none in 1830 Clerics), so the certain fault in the package is the persist omission, which every reload with a team triggers.

Measured on 1,500 combat-backed sorties per configuration, the line is worth deaths: squads in the most timid third die 0.616 per run against 0.682 for the boldest third, and low-morale squads die 0.664 against 0.622.

A squad whose last contract failed, or that went out twice without resting, starts with negative resolve and leaves earlier; a timid squad (low nerve and grit, or cunning) leaves earlier than today in every fight. Measured: deaths per run 0.635 to 0.561 (-12%), the timid third -26% (0.616 to 0.454), the low-morale third -16%, no third rises, win rate 47.6% to 47.1%. Picker rendering is shared with other proposals; partyFacts is the single owner.

Items 1 and 3 are kept as asked; the picker shares an owner with loop-readout through partyFacts. proposals.playerEffect: Any group that has walked out together gets a bonus proportional to its history, and the picker shows it change as members are added or removed. Adding a healer who has not walked with the team lowers the mean gradually (10.9% to 9.1% with one stranger among six) and does not zero it. proposals.secondOrder: Bond events other than 'mission' (shift 0.06, lodging 0.15) still move pair value and accord but not runs, so only walking out together builds rapport, as designed. Grief, tactics trust and cohesion now read one ledger. systems-one-debrief adds 'mission' events for Gate runs, so Gate work builds Field rapport. Fewer places mutate Team state, which removes the case where the Team record disagrees with the roster. Lodging 'one team only' rules and Outfit.teamMembers are unaffected. loop-readout calls Crew.cohesion(gs, party); the signature above is the one to build against.
proposals.risks: The Teams box text ('carried by the people who stay', sortie.js:806) and TEAM_LINE must be rewritten. A team whose rapport came mostly from before the ledger existed, or from runs where only some members went, loses the part the ledger does not support. Lost runs count 0.5 as before. proposals.response: Design attack: the seed rule is min(team.runs, pair.runs), which equals the pair record wherever the ledger is complete, so no migration step is needed and none is added; the 0.5 credit for a lost run is kept through the optional runs weight on the 'mission' event; Gate cohesion is dropped from scope instead of capped, so there is no unmeasured Gate balance change; the picker line is one of the partyFacts entries with a single owner. 'Still a bigger number': the change is to which people the number is attached to and to what feeds it, not its size (maximum unchanged at 18%). Engineering attack: the new signature Crew.cohesion(state, characters) is stated above for loop-readout; it accepts a team object as well so existing callers keep working; cohesion is recomputed on resume, which fixes the dropped bonus and the skipped Crew.completed the antagonist found in persist(); a Node check for it belongs to the headless harness (launch, persist, drop the run, resume, compare the fighter's damage). Deleting Team.runs removes the rapport text that loop-readout reads; it should read co.runs instead.

proposals.title: Give the save undo a control, and replace silent failures with a message
proposals.problem: The import dialog says the replaced save is 'kept, one undo deep', but no control restores it: the rollback key is written and never read. Reset save wipes without keeping anything, and it does not stop a sortie that is running against the old state object. If catalog.json cannot be fetched (game.html opened from disk, or the file missing), init() rejects before any tab handler is attached and the page shows nothing and says nothing. save() swallows storage errors, so a full or blocked store loses progress with no indication.

game.js:2602 import dialog text: 'The save this replaces is kept, one undo deep, until the next import.'

game.js:2679-2681 Reset: state = newState(); save(); nothing kept. sortie.js:294-304 persist() and settle() use run.gs, the old state object; nothing in the Reset path stops the timer, so the run keeps ticking, settle() pays gems into the dead object and writes its log into the new state (Sortie.forget, sortie.js:306, only deletes gs.field.run and does not stop the clock).

game.js:2648-2650 init() awaits LPC.loadCatalog() and Bestiary.loadIndex(); lpc.js:425-428 loadCatalog has no try/catch; game.js:2722 calls init() with no catch. Opened from disk fetch rejects and #content stays empty.
game.js:36-39 save(): catch (e) { /* ignore */ }; game.js:2703 is the only writer of the #tick text.

game.js:31-35 documents the failure that `frozen` prevents (the tick writing the old state back over an imported key); sortie.js beforeunload/visibilitychange call persist(true), which calls G().save(), so any key swap must set frozen first.
Measured save size 3.0 KB per character (182 KB at 60 characters), so one extra copy fits the usual 5 MB quota.
proposals.change:
1) New savestore.js (about 50 lines, IIFE, window.SaveStore and module.exports) holding the two slots over any Storage-like object: replace(storage, key, text) (current becomes rollback, text becomes current; on a quota error returns { ok: false } and leaves the current save as it was), restore(storage, key) (swaps current and rollback, so a restore is itself undoable), wipe(storage, key) (current becomes rollback, current removed; a failed rollback write never blocks the wipe), hasRollback(storage, key). game.js importSave, the Reset handler and the new restore control call it; this is what makes a Node test possible, since game.js cannot be required.
2) openSavePanel (game.js:2535): when a rollback exists, both modes show 'Previous save: N characters, M on the memorial, <town>, G gems' (existing saveSummary/parseSave) and an armed 'Restore previous save' button (arm(), as at game.js:2679). Restore sets frozen = true, calls SaveStore.restore, then location.reload().
3) Reset: before the wipe it calls Sortie.discard() (new, exported next to forget at sortie.js:1387: stop(), run = null, forget(), render(), no settlement), then SaveStore.wipe, then continues as now. The arm text stays 'Wipe everything?'; the panel row above is the undo.
4) init(): wrap the awaited loads in try/catch; on failure write one paragraph into #content: 'catalog.json could not be loaded: <error>. Serve this folder over http (for example: python -m http.server) instead of opening the file directly.'
5) save(): on a storage error remove the rollback key and retry once (the live save outranks the undo copy); if it still fails set a module-level saveError; the 500 ms writer of #tick appends ' - save failed: <error name>' while it is set and clears it after the next successful write.
6) New test/savestore.js with a Map-backed storage stub: replace then restore reproduces the original save byte for byte; restore twice returns to the replaced save; quota on the new write leaves the current save untouched; quota on the rollback write during wipe still wipes; hasRollback is false after a successful restore of an empty rollback.
proposals.playerEffect: A wrong import or an accidental reset can be undone from the panel that warns about it. A player who double-clicks game.html is told what to do instead of seeing an empty shell. A full browser store is visible in the header instead of surfacing later as lost progress. Reset during a sortie no longer leaves a run ticking for characters that no longer exist.
proposals.secondOrder: Reset is no longer irreversible, so the 'Wipe everything?' confirmation protects against misclicks, not data loss. Stored bytes roughly double while a rollback exists; the save() retry drops the rollback first when space runs out. Any later feature that adds a save-time action (autosave slots, export reminders) has one module to extend.
proposals.risks: Restore reloads the page, so frozen must be set before the swap or the tick and sortie persist(true) write the old state back (the failure importSave already documents). Sortie.discard drops a live run without paying or freeing characters on the old state; that is intended because the whole state is being replaced, but it is a new exported function. A very large roster can fail the rollback write; the design accepts that (no undo) instead of failing the wipe.
proposals.response: Design attack (quota, restore without frozen): accepted, both handled in items 1, 2 and 5 and in the test. Engineering demand 1 (Reset leaves the run ticking against the old state): verified in the code (persist and settle both use run.gs, Reset replaces `state`) and added as Sortie.discard(). Demand 2 (drop the rollback on quota): added to save() and wipe. Demand 3 (Node test with a storage stub): needs game.js logic outside game.js, so the slots move to savestore.js; the original plan to test importSave directly was not possible because game.js is an IIFE over the DOM.

Three hook gaps in game-owned files would take effect the day something grants a facet.
evidence: Producers: grep for 'facets' outside the engine finds game.js:86-88 (initialise to [], {}), game.js:413-414 (town tick event, guarded by typeof FacetHostIG) and combat.js:35-39 (FA() accessor); no forge.generate, push or assignment outside tests.

Size: the 15 facet script tags in game.html (facet/*.js 11 files plus facet.quantities, facet.quantities.town, facet.schema, facet.host .ig.js) total 257,017 bytes (computed from the tags); field.html carries the same 15 (grep count 16 'facet' lines in each page).

Hook gap 1: facet/facet.relations.js:260-274 'toll' creates a cell with tier 'mission'; facet.host.ig.js:691 townTierEnd has no caller anywhere (grep), so a mission-tier cell never resets after a sortie.

Hook gap 2: facet.host.ig.js:691-695 townTierEnd returns early without attaching the person record, unlike townEvent at facet.host.ig.js:680-686, so calling it for a character whose record is not yet attached does nothing.

Hook gap 3: combat.js:654 is the only tierEnd call and passes 'encounter'; grep finds no caller of FacetHostIG.detach (facet.host.ig.js:670), so Facet.attached and the host ref table grow by one record per fighter per encounter.

Every game-side call is typeof-guarded (game.js:413, combat.js:38), so removing the script tags leaves the game running as it does now. facet/MANIFEST.json pins the engine files by hash, so the files themselves stay.
proposals.change:

proposals.title: Launching a squad can throw and leave it flagged as out; guard the cause and the ordering
proposals.problem: Missions.prepare throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading stacked)' when a character's class teaches words whose minimum arcana level is above the character's arcana level and the character is not born to arcana. sortie.launch has already set c.mission, assigned run and (for a trial) spent the trial cost by then, so the party reads 'already out', the run screen has no timer, and the only recovery is a reload. Reachable for 1- and 2-star Clerics and Alchemists whose stats or aptitudes were raised to meet the class requirement.
evidence: Stack (reproduced in Node): TypeError at spellcraft.js:109 masteredTier <- :366 tierTok <- :370 randomSentence <- :409 generate <- ai.js:131 decide. spellcraft.js:363 `usable = lexicon.filter(id => WORDS[id].minLevel <= level)` is empty, R.pick(usable) is undefined, WORDS[undefined] is read.
missions.js:104-128 prepare builds a grimoire whenever Sp.lexiconOf(c).length is non-zero; it does not check that any word is usable at the character's arcana level.

sortie.js:198-266 launch(): Quests.begin spends the trial cost (quests.js:165-175) at ~line 214; run is assigned at ~line 253; c.mission = id at line 263; fighterFor (which calls M.prepare) at line 265; G().save() and start() after. There is no try/catch, so a throw leaves c.mission set and run non-null with no timer; sortie.js:1069 only handles a string return.

Reachability, measured (scratchpad cleanup2/crash4.js, crash7.js): characters made eligible for Cleric or Alchemist by the real Classes.eligible check, with no arcana gift: 3, 4 and 5 stars, over 5,000 eligible characters, 0 throw. 1 star with WIS raised to 14 and the prerequisite aptitude at E-: 208 of 809 Clerics and 122 of 316 Alchemists throw; 2 stars: 73 of 1608 and 139 of 865. Stats can be raised by sacrifice (sacrifice.js:165 adds a spent character's base stats to the target) and aptitudes by advancement. The training dropdown calls Classes.assign without force (game.js:1972).

A force-assigned class (Classes.assign with force) throws for about 1 in 3 one-star Clerics and Alchemists; this is not reachable in play and I did not use it as evidence. A specialisation reached through Classes.specialise throws in 1 of 15,957 sampled characters (mutagenic grown from alchemist).
proposals.change:
1) spellcraft.js randomSentence: return [] when usable is empty (checkSentence then rejects it and generate() returns null, which AI.decide already handles at ai.js:131-140). That removes the throw for every class and level.
2) missions.js prepare: no change needed after (1); add a comment stating that an empty usable lexicon yields an empty grimoire.
3) sortie.js launch(): wrap the fighterFor loop in try/catch. On a throw: run = null, c.mission = null for the party, refund the trial cost (gs[k] += paid[k] for the keys Quests.begin deducted), and return the string 'Could not prepare <name>: <message>' so the existing problem text at sortie.js:1069-1070 shows it.
4) New test/prepare.js (Node): for stars 1 to 5, for every base class, raise stats and prerequisite aptitudes until Classes.eligible is true, over 200 characters each, Missions.prepare must not throw; Spellcraft.randomSentence on an empty lexicon returns [].
proposals.playerEffect: A squad that cannot cast anything at its arcana level launches with a plain martial plan instead of locking its members until a reload. A trial cost is not lost if fighter preparation fails.
proposals.secondOrder: A low-level Cleric or Alchemist becomes a martial-only fighter until its arcana level reaches the first word it was taught, which is how a class-taught word below the player's level is already treated. The launch guard turns any later preparation error into a message and keeps the board and the roster consistent.
proposals.risks: The test raises stats and aptitudes synthetically; it shows the code path throws and that the guard prevents it, not how often a real roster reaches it. Refund logic must use exactly the items Quests.begin deducted (the `paid` object it returns).
proposals.response: This is the one proposal added from the 'missed' list: both attackers listed this crash and no builder owned it. I reproduced it, and corrected its reach: the attackers' figures (22 of 50 one-star Clerics, 7 of 400 random characters) came from force-assigned classes; with the real eligibility check there are 0 throws among more than 5,000 eligible 3-5 star characters and a high rate only among 1-2 star characters whose stats were raised. It is still worth fixing because the failure state persists until reload and, on a trial launch, costs the trial fee.
